text: When the dance finally stopped. <break time="0.8s" /> He knocked at the door. <break time="0.8s" /> And Shepherd Fennel. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was a kind and generous host. <break time="0.8s" /> Opened it at once. <break time="0.8s" /> May I come in and rest a little while. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked the stranger politely. <break time="0.8s" /> Explaining that the rain had made the road. <break time="0.8s" /> Almost impossible to walk on. <break time="0.8s" /> The shepherd welcomed him warmly. <break time="0.8s" /> And said that he had chosen a good night to visit. <break time="0.8s" /> Since they were celebrating. <break time="0.8s" /> A happy event in the family. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting by the warm fire. <break time="0.8s" /> The stranger gladly accepted some tobacco. <break time="0.8s" /> But he had to borrow a pipe as well. <break time="0.8s" /> Saying that he had dropped his own. <break time="0.8s" /> The shepherd thought it odd. <break time="0.8s" /> That a smoker should carry no pipe. <break time="0.8s" /> But the stranger quietly lit his borrowed one. <break time="0.8s" /> And warmed himself in silence. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon there came a second knock. <break time="0.8s" /> And a few moments later. <break time="0.8s" /> Another man stood dripping in the doorway. <break time="0.8s" /> Asking to be let in out of the storm. <break time="0.8s" /> He was a rather stout man. <break time="0.8s" /> Dressed in a suit of cinder gray cloth. <break time="0.8s" /> Who seemed several years older. <break time="0.8s" /> Than the first stranger. <break time="0.8s" /> Without waiting to be invited twice. <break time="0.8s" /> He took off his wet coat. <break time="0.8s" /> And sat down by the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> Close to the man who had come first.
